# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 36 BEAUTY FOR ASHES

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Is there any news coming from Grey Shutters, Nell?”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0000 }

“Nothing very especial,” answered Nell, putting away the letter from Thirza. “Jake Trask has been at the place putting shingles on the roof. He is now a fully trained carpenter, so he appears to have achieved his desire concerning his chosen profession. You recall that his mother desired a college professor's career for him. That day she arrived at the school and scolded me because I did not address him as St. Clair will always remain in my memory.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0001 }

“Is he ever called that by anyone nowadays?”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0002 }

“Clearly he has not. He appears to have moved past it entirely. His mother has even given in. My belief was always that a young man possessing Jake’s mouth and chin would ultimately prevail. Isolde informs me in a letter that a beau has been found by Lucy. Reflect upon that—a child like her!”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0003 }

“Lucy’s age is seventeen,” Hugh said. “Both Wilfred Mott and I were crazy for you when your age was seventeen, Nell.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0004 }

“In truth, Hugh, we are certainly aging,” remarked Nell, displaying a somewhat mournful grin, “if kids who were merely six years old back when we considered ourselves adults have reached an age to attract suitors. Lucy’s companion is Ralph Pullen—the brother of Odette. My memory of him is as a small, plump, heavy-set, fair-haired boy who consistently stayed at the bottom of his grade. However, I hear that he has grown into a rather handsome youth today.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0005 }

“It is likely that Lucy is going to wed at an early age. Her nature resembles that of Belinda the Fourth—she will certainly seize her initial opportunity out of dread that a second one may not arrive.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0006 }

“Well; if Ralph becomes her husband, my wish is that he shows a bit more ambition than Barney, his brother,” reflected Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0007 }

“As an example,” Hugh said with a laugh, “we can pray that he manages to make a proposal for himself. Nell, if Barney had popped the question directly, rather than having Odette act as his messenger, would you have accepted him?”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0008 }

“I could have.” Nell burst into a shrill laugh as she remembered her initial proposal. “Being so shocked by everything could have mesmerized me into doing something so reckless and silly. We should be grateful that he used a surrogate.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0009 }

“Yesterday, a letter arrived for me from Laurence Vane,” Lorna mentioned out of the corner where she sat reading.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0010 }

“Oh, how is he?” Nell inquired with interest, though she felt strangely as if the person she was asking about was a stranger to her.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0011 }

“He is fine, though adjusting to every change regarding his former home and companions proves extremely difficult for him. Once spring arrives, he will return to the sea. He claims it is in his blood, and he yearns to be back on it. However, he shared a piece of news that brought me happiness on his behalf, poor man. Prior to departing on the Four Sisters, he had been betrothed to a local girl. He refrained from mentioning her to me in Montreal, explaining that he assumed she would have put him out of her mind and wed another man years ago, whereas for him, the betrothal and affection remained entirely current. Though this was quite painful for him, his return home revealed that she had remained unmarried and still held affection for him. Their wedding is planned for this autumn. I intend to invite him to bring her here for a brief visit; he mentions a desire to come observe the location where he resided for so many years unaware.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0012 }

“What a sweet little love story,” remarked Nell, who possessed an undying fondness for romance. “And to consider,” she continued while sighing remorsefully, “that Laurence Vane would have remained in the grave where his true self was entombed had I gotten what I wanted. I battled so fiercely against the idea Hugh had! Well, my retribution has arrived: never again will I be permitted to disagree with Hugh! Should I attempt to, he will crush me by bringing up Laurence Vane’s situation!”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0013 }

“Even that wouldn't hush a woman!” Hugh scoffed. “At any rate, Nell, stop echoing me. Life is made more interesting with a bit of disagreement. My desire is not for a spouse resembling John MacAllister’s across the harbor. Whatever statement he makes, she immediately observes in her dull, spiritless small voice, 'That is very true, John, dear me!’”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0014 }

Nell and Lorna giggled. A musical perfection like a flawless chord was created by blending Nell’s silvery laugh with the golden tone of Lorna’s.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0015 }

Tabitha, entering right after the laughter occurred, mirrored it by letting out a deep sigh.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0016 }

“Why, Tabitha, what is wrong?” Hugh inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0017 }

“Little Kit isn’t unwell, is he, Tabitha?” Nell shouted, leaping up in fright.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0018 }

“No, no, settle down, Mrs. Doctor, dear. A thing has occurred, however. Dear me, all things have gone completely wrong for me during this week. I ruined the bread, as you are only too aware—and I burned the doctor’s finest shirt bosom—and I shattered your large platter. And now, to cap it all off, news arrives that my sister Matilda has fractured her leg and desires that I travel to remain with her for a time.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0019 }

“Oh, I am deeply sorry—that is to say, sorry that your sister suffered such a mishap,” cried Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0020 }

“Ah, well, human beings were created to grieve, Mrs. Doctor, dear. It seems like something that should belong in the Bible, yet I am informed that an individual called Burns composed it. Furthermore, it is certainly true that we are destined for sorrow just as sparks ascend. Regarding Matilda, I am at a loss as to what I should believe about her. Never before has any member of our family fractured a leg. Nevertheless, regardless of her actions, she remains my sister, and I believe it is my obligation to travel there and attend to her, provided you are able to manage without me for a couple of weeks, Mrs. Doctor, dear.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0021 }

“Naturally, Tabitha, naturally. Someone else can be found to assist me during your absence.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0022 }

“Should you be unable to, I shall refrain from attending, Mrs. Doctor, dear, despite Matilda’s leg. I refuse to cause you anxiety, and to have that sweet child disturbed as a result, for all the legs in existence.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0023 }

“Oh, Tabitha, you ought to travel to your sister immediately. I am able to obtain a girl from the cove, who will manage for now.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0024 }

“Nell, will you allow me to come and live with you during Tabitha’s absence?” Lorna cried out. “Please do! I’d delight in it—and you would be performing a charitable deed. I am so terribly isolated over there inside that large barn-like home. I have so few tasks to occupy me—and during the night I am more than just isolated—I am scared and edgy even with the doors secured. A tramp was lurking about two days back.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0025 }

Nell delightfully accepted, and on the following day, Lorna took up residence in the modest house of dreams. Miss Winifred enthusiastically favored the plan.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0026 }

“It appears to be Providential,” she privately remarked to Nell. “I feel regret for Matilda Clow, yet given that breaking her leg was unavoidable, the timing could not have been superior. Lorna is going to reside here during the period that Adrian Treleaven remains in Seven Gulls, preventing those old cats up at the Glen from having an opportunity to meow, which they certainly would if she were residing over there by herself while Adrian visited her. They are already engaging in enough gossip because of her refusal to wear mourning clothes. I observed to one among them, 'If you imply that she ought to wear mourning clothes for Laurence Vane, it strikes me as resembling his resurrection far more than his funeral; whereas if you are referring to Rufus, I admit I fail to perceive the appropriateness of wearing weeds for an individual who passed away thirteen years back, whose departure was a good riddance at the time!’ Furthermore, when old Louisa Baldwin commented to me that she considered it extremely odd for Lorna to have never harbored a suspicion that he was not her actual husband, I replied, 'YOU failed to ever suspect he was not Rufus Vane, despite being his next-door neighbor throughout his entire existence, and by temperament you possess ten times more suspicion than Lorna.’ Nevertheless, one is unable to silence certain individuals' tongues, Nell, dearie, and I feel truly grateful that Lorna will reside beneath your roof throughout the time Adrian is courting her.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0027 }

On an August evening, Adrian Treleaven arrived at the small home while Lorna and Nell were fully occupied with doting on the infant. Unobserved by the pair inside, he stopped at the open doorway of the living room, taking in the lovely scene with hungry eyes. Lorna was seated on the carpet holding the baby on her lap, delightedly touching his chubby little hands as he waved them about in the air.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0028 }

“Oh, you dear, beautiful, beloved baby,” she murmured, grabbing a tiny hand and pressing kisses all over it.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0029 }

“Is he not the most darling little thing,” Nell murmured, leaning over her chair's arm in adoration. “Those little tiny pads are the sweetest hands in the entire wide world, are they not, you darling little man.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0030 }

Nell, during the months preceding the arrival of Little Kit, had studied several erudite books with great diligence, and she placed her trust particularly in one, “Sir Oracle on the Care and Training of Children.” Parents were implored by Sir Oracle, by everything they deemed sacred, never to speak “baby talk” to their offspring. From the very moment they are born, infants must always be spoken to in classical language. Thus would they acquire the ability to utter pure English from their very first words. “How,” Sir Oracle inquired, “can a mother reasonably expect her child to learn correct speech, when she continually accustoms its impressionable gray matter to such absurd expressions and distortions of our noble tongue as thoughtless mothers inflict every day on the helpless creatures committed to their care? Can a child who is constantly called 'tweet itty wee singie’ ever attain to any proper conception of his own being and possibilities and destiny?”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0031 }

This left a deep impression on Nell, who told Hugh that she intended to establish a strict rule to never, no matter what, use “baby talk” with her offspring. Hugh concurred with her, leading them to form a serious pact regarding the matter—a agreement that Nell flagrantly broke as soon as Little Kit was placed in her embrace. “Oh, the darling itty wee sing!” she had cried out. Furthermore, she had persisted in breaking it from that time onward. Whenever Hugh mocked her, she treated Sir Oracle with complete contempt.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0032 }

“Hugh, he was without any offspring himself—I am certain he lacked them, otherwise he could not have penned such nonsense. Speaking baby talk to an infant is simply unavoidable. It happens instinctively—and it is PROPER. Addressing those small, gentle, downy little beings the way we address large boys and girls would be heartless. Infants require affection, embraces, and every bit of sweet baby talk available to them, and Little Kit will receive it, bless his sweet itty heartums.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0033 }

“However, you are the most terrible I ever listened to, Nell,” objected Hugh, who, since he was merely a father rather than a mother, had not been completely persuaded yet that Sir Oracle was mistaken. “The manner in which you speak to that child is unlike anything I ever listened to.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0034 }

“It is highly probable that you never did. Leave—leave. Before reaching eleven years of age, did I not raise three sets of Rudge twins? Sir Oracle and you are merely dispassionate theorists. Hugh, ONLY take a glance at him! He is grinning in my direction—he understands what is being discussed by us. And oo dest agwees wif evy word muzzer says, don’t oo, angel-lover?”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0035 }

Hugh wrapped an arm around the pair. “Ah, all of you mothers!” he remarked. “You mothers! When God created you, He certainly knew what He was doing.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0036 }

Thus Little Kit received speeches, affection, and hugs; and he grew well as was fitting for a infant from the home of dreams. Lorna displayed just as much folly regarding him as Nell did. Once their chores were finished and Hugh had departed, they surrendered to unabashed sprees of affection and fits of worship, like the one where Adrian Treleaven had caught them unawares.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0037 }

Lorna noticed him before anyone else did. Even as the light faded, Nell was able to observe the abrupt paleness that spread across her lovely face, erasing the red color from her lips and cheeks.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0038 }

Adrian stepped toward us, full of eagerness, briefly taking no notice of Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0039 }

“Lorna!” he uttered, extending his hand. Never before had he addressed her by her first name; yet the hand Lorna proffered him felt cold; and throughout the entire evening she remained extremely quiet, whereas Nell and Hugh and Adrian shared laughter and conversation. She made her excuses and ascended the stairs prior to the conclusion of his visit. The cheerful mood Adrian possessed waned, and he departed shortly thereafter looking disheartened.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0040 }

Hugh's eyes turned toward Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0041 }

“Nell, what are you doing? There is something happening that escapes my understanding. Tonight, the entire atmosphere in this place has been filled with tension. Lorna is seated resembling the muse of tragedy; Adrian Treleaven makes jokes and laughs outwardly, while observing Lorna with his soul's eyes. You appear constantly on the verge of exploding with a hidden excitement. Confess. What secret have you been hiding from your misled husband?”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0042 }

“Do not be silly, Hugh,” Nell answered her husband. “Regarding Lorna, she is ridiculous, and I am heading upstairs to inform her of that.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0043 }

Nell discovered Lorna located at the dormer window belonging to her room. The rhythmic thunder of the ocean filled the small space. Lorna was sitting with clasped hands in the misty moonlight—a lovely, accusing presence.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0044 }

“Nell,” she uttered quietly and critically, “were you aware that Adrian Treleaven was traveling to Seven Gulls?”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0045 }

“I did,” Nell stated without shame.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0046 }

“Oh, Nell, you ought to have informed me,” Lorna exclaimed with intensity. “Had I been aware, I’d have left—I’d not have remained in this place to encounter him. You ought to have informed me. You weren’t being fair, Nell—oh, you weren’t being fair!”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0047 }

Lorna’s entire body was stiffened by feeling, and her lips shuddered. Nell, however, uttered a cruel laugh. She leaned down to place a kiss upon Lorna’s turned-up, accusatory face.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0048 }

“Lorna, you are an adorable goose. Adrian Treleaven didn’t hurry from the Pacific to the Atlantic out of a desperate craving to see ME. I also do not think that he was motivated by any fierce and frantic devotion to Miss Winifred. Shed your tragic demeanour, my dear friend, and fold it up and store it away in lavender. You will not require it ever again. There are certain individuals who are capable of seeing through a grindstone when a hole exists in it, even though you are unable to. I do not claim to be a prophetess, yet I will risk making a forecast. Life’s bitterness has come to an end for you. From now on you will experience the delights and expectations—and I imagine the griefs, as well—of a contented woman. The omen of the shadow of Venus really did come to pass for you, Lorna. The year when you witnessed it delivered your life’s finest present to you—your love for Adrian Treleaven. Now, retire straight to bed and get a restful sleep.”
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0049 }

Lorna conformed to instructions to the extent that she retired to bed, though it is doubtful whether she enjoyed much sleep. I doubt she permitted herself to indulge in daydreams; existence had proven so difficult for this unfortunate Lorna, and the route she was forced to tread had been so narrow, that she was unable to murmur to her inner self the expectations that the times ahead might hold. Nevertheless, she observed the immense rotating beacon ornamenting the brief hours of the summer darkness with star-like brightness, and a youthful, soft, and luminous quality returned to her eyes. Furthermore, she did not refuse Adrian Treleaven when he arrived the following day to request her company for a visit to the beach.
{: #nw-v04-c36-p0050 }
